subtopics.title: Calculate the mid-point
subtopics.exposition: The mid-point of a line segment between two points A(x1, y1) and B(x2, y2) is denoted M(x, y). The mid-point of a line is M(x, y) = ((x1+x2)/2, (y1+y2)/2). To calculate the mid-point of a line between two given end points: draw a sketch of the two points to estimate the sign and position of the mid-point; assign the end points' coordinates to x1, y1, x2, y2; write down the mid-point formula; substitute the assigned values and simplify to find x and y; then compare the calculated mid-point to the sketch estimate. Coordinates of a point are written as an ordered pair with a semicolon separating the x- and y-values, e.g. P(2, 1), not a comma.

subtopics.title: Find an unknown endpoint
subtopics.exposition: To find an unknown end point given the mid-point and the other end point: write down the mid-point formula with the known mid-point coordinates and the known end point's coordinates substituted in, then solve the resulting equations for the unknown x- and y-coordinates of the other end point.

subtopics.title: Find a parallelogram vertex
subtopics.exposition: The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other. To find an unknown vertex H of a parallelogram EFGH: calculate the mid-point of one diagonal (EG) using the mid-point formula; since the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, this is also the mid-point of the other diagonal (FH); substitute this mid-point and the known vertex F into the mid-point formula and solve for the coordinates of H.
